name: pretty-math
description: Renders the math expression under your cursor as real two-dimensional math in a panel, so precedence and grouping mistakes are obvious.

prettyMath.autoUpdate.description: Re-render automatically as the cursor moves or the selection changes.

prettyMath.fontSize.description: Base font size (px) of the rendered math.

prettyMath.caretMeansPower.markdownDescription: How to read `^`. `auto` uses the language: power in MATLAB/Julia/R/Lua/Fortran, bitwise XOR in C/C++/C#/Java/JavaScript/Python/Rust/Go.

prettyMath.multiplication.markdownDescription: How to draw `*`. `implicit` juxtaposes factors (a dot is still inserted where it would be ambiguous).

prettyMath.indexAsSubscript.markdownDescription: Render `a[i]` as a subscript rather than with brackets.

prettyMath.greekLetters.markdownDescription: Render identifiers named after Greek letters (`theta`, `omega`, `dt_alpha`, ...) as the letter itself.

prettyMath.expandIdentities.markdownDescription: Expand a few library calls into the math they stand for: `hypot(a,b)` as a root, `log1p(x)` as ln(1+x), `expm1(x)` as e^x-1, `exp(x)` as e^x.

prettyMath.derivativeSymbol.markdownDescription: The symbol used for a derivative. `auto` writes `d` for a single variable and `∂` when several are differentiated.

prettyMath.stripNamespaces.markdownDescription: Qualifiers dropped before rendering, so `np.sqrt(x)` reads as a plain root and `self.mass` as `mass`.

prettyMath.substituteValues.markdownDescription: Draw what the variables are worth in place of their names. Values come from a paused debug session when there is one, otherwise from assignments above the cursor, which are read but never executed. Toggled by the **Values** button in the panel.

prettyMath.jupyterValues.markdownDescription: In a notebook, ask the running kernel what the variables hold, the way the Variables view does. **Off by default**: the Jupyter extension will ask you to grant this extension permission to execute code against kernels, which is a broad permission for a narrow use, so it is opt-in. What gets sent is a single statement that prints the names currently holding a finite number and defines nothing. Only applies while **Values** is on, and only where a kernel is already idle. Without it, values still come from the cells above.

prettyMath.mathInput.markdownDescription: Turn names into symbols as you type them: `\alpha` becomes α, `\int` becomes ∫, `\le` becomes ≤. The name is replaced once you type something that cannot be part of it, so both `\le` and `\leq` can be reached, and a space used only to end a name is swallowed. Nothing without a leading backslash is ever touched. Toggled with **Alt+Shift+M**.

prettyMath.mathInputTarget.markdownDescription: What **Format Selection as Math** (Alt+M) writes. `auto` writes LaTeX between dollar signs in a notebook's markdown cell, a `.md` file or a LaTeX document, where it will be rendered as real two-dimensional maths, and Unicode such as `x² + √y` everywhere else, where a backslash would only ever be read as a backslash.

prettyMath.showChecks.markdownDescription: Report what is wrong with the formula as well as drawing it: units that do not match, and a short list of mistakes that are certain rather than suspected. Toggled by the **Checks** button in the panel.

prettyMath.checkUnits.markdownDescription: Check that the quantities in a formula can be combined: that an energy is not added to a pressure, and that nothing with units is handed to `exp` or `sin`. Units are known from `scipy.constants` and from any unit you write in a trailing comment, as in `T = 300  # K`. A name whose units cannot be traced is left alone, so nothing is guessed.

prettyMath.lintFormulas.markdownDescription: Point out mistakes that are certain: degrees handed to a function that wants radians, equality between floating-point numbers, `-2**2`, integer division that truncates, a comparison chain in a language that has none, and a bit mask compared before it is applied.

prettyMath.valueDigits.description: Significant digits used when a substituted value is not a whole number.

prettyMath.showLatex.description: Show the LaTeX source underneath the rendered math.

prettyMath.showTree.description: Show the parse tree underneath the rendered math.

prettyMath.maxLines.description: Maximum number of statements rendered from a multi-line selection.

scripts.test: node test/run.js && node test/host.js && node test/corpus.js && node test/libraries.js && node test/checks.js && node test/mathinput.js && node test/hostile.js && node test/fuzz.js
